title: What is cohesion, why is HIGH cohesion a design goal (SRP — each class does one thing), and what does LOW cohesion look like (God class doing unrelated tasks)?
shortTitle: What is cohesion and why is high cohesion a design goal?

s1_definition.profdef: COHESION measures how closely related the responsibilities within a SINGLE class are. HIGH COHESION: all methods and fields serve ONE clear purpose — `FeeCalculator` only calculates fees (SRP — Single Responsibility Principle). LOW COHESION: the class does many UNRELATED things — a "God class" `BankingManager` that handles accounts, trades, notifications, reports, and compliance in one 3000-line class. HIGH cohesion is the goal because: each class is easy to understand (one purpose), easy to test (test one thing), easy to change (modify fees without touching notifications), and easy to reuse (use FeeCalculator in any service).
s1_definition.analogy: HIGH COHESION: the bank has SEPARATE counters — one for deposits, one for loans, one for forex. Each counter does ONE thing well. Need to change loan processing? Only the loan counter changes. DEPOSIT counter unaffected. LOW COHESION: one clerk handles deposits, loans, forex, complaints, and makes coffee — overwhelmed, error-prone, and if the clerk is sick, EVERYTHING stops. That clerk is a "God class."
s1_definition.oneliner: High cohesion = one class, one purpose, all methods related (SRP). Low cohesion = God class, many unrelated responsibilities. Strive for: HIGH cohesion + LOOSE coupling = clean design.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** COHESION measures how closely related the responsibilities within a SINGLE class are. HIGH COHESION: all methods and fields serve ONE clear purpose — `FeeCalculator` only calculates fees (SRP — Single Responsibility Principle). LOW COHESION: the class does many UNRELATED things — a "God class" `BankingManager` that handles accounts, trades, notifications, reports, and compliance in one 3000-line class. HIGH cohesion is the goal because: each class is easy to understand (one purpose), easy to test (test one thing), easy to change (modify fees without touching notifications), and easy to reuse (use FeeCalculator in any service).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** HIGH COHESION: the bank has SEPARATE counters — one for deposits, one for loans, one for forex. Each counter does ONE thing well. Need to change loan processing? Only the loan counter changes. DEPOSIT counter unaffected. LOW COHESION: one clerk handles deposits, loans, forex, complaints, and makes coffee — overwhelmed, error-prone, and if the clerk is sick, EVERYTHING stops. That clerk is a "God class."

**One line to remember:** High cohesion = one class, one purpose, all methods related (SRP). Low cohesion = God class, many unrelated responsibilities. Strive for: HIGH cohesion + LOOSE coupling = clean design.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank's 3000-line `BankingManager` God class handles accounts, trades, fees, notifications, and compliance.** Bug report: "fee calculation is wrong for intraday trades." Developer opens BankingManager — 3000 lines, 50 methods. Takes 2 hours to find the fee methods buried between notification code and compliance checks. Fixes the fee bug but accidentally breaks the SMS notification method (copy-paste error in the same file). The fix: decompose into 5 cohesive classes. Each class: 50-200 lines, one purpose, independently testable.
sections.s4a_structure:
```
cohesion-service/
├── src/
│   ├── main/java/com/bank/cohesion/
│   │   ├── bad/
│   │   │   └── GodClass.java                (LOW cohesion)
│   │   ├── good/
│   │   │   ├── AccountService.java          (HIGH — accounts only)
│   │   │   ├── FeeCalculator.java           (HIGH — fees only)
│   │   │   ├── NotificationService.java     (HIGH — notifications only)
│   │   │   └── TradeOrchestrator.java       (coordinates cohesive services)
│   └── test/java/com/bank/cohesion/

```

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 — God class.** Developer opens 3000-line BankingManager to fix a fee bug. Scrolls past account methods, trade methods, notification methods — finally finds fee calculation at line 2100. Fixes it. Accidentally modifies the sendSms method two lines below (copy-paste). Notification broken.

**Step 2 — Decompose.** Split into: AccountService (accounts), FeeCalculator (fees), NotificationService (notifications), TradeExecutionService (trades), ComplianceService (compliance). Each: 50-200 lines.

**Step 3 — Fix fee bug.** Open FeeCalculator — 30 lines. Fee methods only. Fix in 5 minutes. IMPOSSIBLE to break notifications — they're in a DIFFERENT class.

**Step 4 — Test fees.** `new FeeCalculator()` — test in isolation. No account/trade/notification code loaded. 10ms. God class test: loads everything even for one fee test — slow, fragile.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ LOW COHESION (God Class) ═══

  BankingManager (3000 lines):
  ├─ createAccount()        ┐
  ├─ getBalance()           │ Accounts
  ├─ closeAccount()         ┘
  ├─ executeTrade()         ┐ Trades
  ├─ cancelTrade()          ┘
  ├─ calculateBrokerage()   ┐ Fees
  ├─ calculateGST()         ┘
  ├─ sendSms()              ┐ Notifications
  ├─ sendEmail()            ┘
  ├─ checkKYC()             ┐ Compliance
  └─ submitRBIReport()      ┘
  5 UNRELATED responsibilities in ONE class → LOW cohesion!

  ═══ HIGH COHESION (Decomposed) ═══

  AccountService (50 lines): createAccount, getBalance, closeAccount
  FeeCalculator (30 lines): brokerage, gst, totalFees
  NotificationService (20 lines): sendSms, sendEmail
  TradeService (40 lines): executeTrade, cancelTrade
  ComplianceService (30 lines): checkKYC, submitRBIReport

  Each class: ONE purpose. Independently testable. Easy to change.

  ═══ THE "AND" TEST ═══
  Low:  "manages accounts AND trades AND fees AND notifications" → SPLIT!
  High: "calculates trading fees" → DONE! No "AND."
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  LOW COHESION (anti-pattern):
  ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │ BankManager  (God class)    │
  │ + createAccount()           │
  │ + calculateFee()            │  5 unrelated
  │ + executeTrade()            │  responsibilities
  │ + sendNotification()        │  = hard to test/change
  │ + checkCompliance()         │
  └────────────────────────────┘

  HIGH COHESION (SRP refactor):
  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐
  │ AccountService │  │ FeeCalculator  │
  │ + create()     │  │ + calcFee(txn) │
  │ + close()      │  └────────────────┘
  └────────────────┘
  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐
  │ TradeService   │  │ NotifyService  │
  │ + execute()    │  │ + send(msg)    │
  └────────────────┘  └────────────────┘

  SOLID: SRP = one reason to change per class
  Benefits: testable, changeable, reusable
  Call chain: AccountService.create()
              → FeeCalculator.calcFee()
              → NotifyService.send()
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Cohesion measures how closely related the responsibilities within a single class are. High cohesion means all methods and fields serve ONE clear purpose — FeeCalculator only calculates fees, AccountService only manages accounts. Low cohesion means the class does many unrelated things — the "God class" anti-pattern with 3000 lines handling accounts, trades, fees, notifications, and compliance. High cohesion is a design goal because it enables: understandability (one purpose = easy to read), testability (test one thing in isolation), changeability (modify fees without touching notifications), and reusability (use FeeCalculator anywhere without dragging unrelated code).

In my banking service, the GodClass has 8 methods across 5 unrelated areas. Testing fee calculation requires instantiating the entire God class — including account, trade, and notification code. Fixing a fee bug risks breaking notifications (same file, same class). The decomposed version: 5 cohesive classes, each 30-50 lines. FeeCalculator tested alone in 10ms. Fix fee bug: open 30-line FeeCalculator, modify, done. NotificationService: untouched, safe. Different developers work on different files — no merge conflicts.

The "AND" test: describe the class in one sentence. If you use "AND" — the class has too many responsibilities, split it. "BankingManager manages accounts AND executes trades AND calculates fees AND sends notifications" → four "AND"s = four classes needed. "FeeCalculator calculates trading fees" → no "AND" = high cohesion. The ideal design: HIGH cohesion (focused classes) + LOOSE coupling (interfaces + DI) = clean, maintainable, testable code.
